title: Mixed-corner sign-reversing involution for evaluated shuffle paths
statement:
For any set $S$, let $\mathbf Z[S]$ be the free $\mathbf Z$-module with basis $S$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; evaluated strings below can equivalently be read as basis symbols in the free module on strings of their length. Let $a,b\geq0$, $n=a+b$, and let $W_{a,b}$ be the finite set of words $w_0\cdots w_{n-1}$ with $a$ letters $H$ and $b$ letters $V$. Put $A_k(w)=\#\{r<k:w_r=H\}$ and $B_k(w)=\#\{r<k:w_r=V\}$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $I(w)=\#\{(r,s):r<s,\ w_r=V,\ w_s=H\}$ and $s(w)=(-1)^{I(w)}\in\mathbf Z$. For any sets $X,Y$ and sequences $u=(u_0,\ldots,u_a)$ in $X$, $v=(v_0,\ldots,v_b)$ in $Y$, write $z_{u,v}(w)=((u_{A_k(w)},v_{B_k(w)}))_{k=0}^n$ and let $d_k$ denote deletion of entry $k$ of a sequence. No distinctness of sequence entries is assumed.

Let $\pi_w$ be the permutation of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ whose list consists first of the $H$ positions, increasingly, then of the $V$ positions, increasingly. Its inversion count is exactly $I(w)$, and its permutation sign is $s(w)$. Suppose $n>0$ and set $M_{a,b}=\{(w,k):w\in W_{a,b},\ 0<k<n,\ w_{k-1}\ne w_k\}$. On this set, swapping letters $k-1,k$ and leaving $k$ fixed defines a fixed-point-free involution $\tau(w,k)=(w',k)$. The coordinate paths $(A_\ell,B_\ell)$ for $w,w'$ agree at every $\ell\ne k$, and their inversion counts differ by $1$. In particular
$$d_kz_{u,v}(w')=d_kz_{u,v}(w),\qquad s(w')(-1)^k=-s(w)(-1)^k.$$
Consequently, in the free abelian group on length-$n$ sequences in $X\times Y$,
$$\sum_{(w,k)\in M_{a,b}}s(w)(-1)^k[d_kz_{u,v}(w)]=0.$$
If $a=0$ or $b=0$, $M_{a,b}$ is empty.

Blueprint gives the application, not this combinatorial lemma. WANTED: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, §8.5 (not available locally).

proof.text: The increasing lists of H positions and V positions partition the n positions, so their concatenation defines the bijection $\pi_w$. Within either list there are no inversions. A cross-list inversion has values $h>v$ with $w_h=H,w_v=V$; sending it to $(v,h)$ is a bijection onto the pairs counted by $I(w)$. Thus the inversion count of $\pi_w$ is $I(w)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle input: permutation encoding, expanded by Q158.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-permutation-sign-inversion-product] to $\pi_w$. Its product has a factor $-1$ exactly for each inversion counted in step 1; every other factor is $1$. Removing the factors $1$ leaves $I(w)$ identical factors $-1$, whose product is $(-1)^{I(w)}=s(w)$. This also gives sign $1$ for the empty permutation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle input: identify the shuffle sign.

proof.text: Fix $(w,k)\in M_{a,b}$ and put $p=k-1$. The two letters at $p,k$ are H,V in some order. Interchanging them preserves the counts a,b and leaves the pair mixed, so $(w\prime,k)$ lies in $M_{a,b}$. A second interchange restores every letter. The letter at p changes, so $w\prime\ne w$ and $\tau$ has no fixed point. If $a=0$ or $b=0$, every letter is the same, so no such mixed pair exists and $M_{a,b}$ is empty.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle input: define the labeled mixed-corner involution.

proof.text: For $\ell\leq p$, the prefixes of length $\ell$ contain neither swapped position and agree. For $\ell\geq k+1$, they contain both, with one H and one V in either order, and hence have the same two counts. These ranges are exactly $\ell\ne k$. Thus every retained vertex has the same coordinate indices for $w,w\prime$. At position t after deleting entry k, the original index is t if $t<k$ and $t+1$ if $t\geq k$; both avoid k. Evaluating u,v therefore gives $d_kz_{u,v}(w\prime)=d_kz_{u,v}(w)$ without requiring either sequence to be injective.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle input: equality of the deleted evaluated strings.

proof.text: For inversions under this swap, pairs disjoint from $\{p,k\}$ are unchanged. For each position $r<p$, the sum of its contributions with p and k is unchanged: if $w_r=V$ it is one, and if $w_r=H$ it is zero. For each $s>k$, the contributions from p and k to s likewise sum to one when $w_s=H$ and zero when $w_s=V$. No position lies strictly between p and k. The sole remaining pair $(p,k)$ contributes zero for HV and one for VH. Consequently $I(w\prime)=I(w)+1$ in the HV case and $I(w)=I(w\prime)+1$ in the VH case. In either case $(-1)^{m+1}=-(-1)^m$ gives $s(w\prime)=-s(w)$, and multiplication by $(-1)^k$ gives the asserted coefficient identity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written universal shuffle input: explicit inversion-pair count at a mixed corner.

proof.text: The set $M_{a,b}$ is finite: it is a subset of the finite set of binary words of length n times the n+1 possible vertex indices. In the free module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on length-n strings define $f(w,k)=s(w)(-1)^k[d_kz_{u,v}(w)]$. Steps 4–5 give $f(w,k)+f(\tau(w,k))=c[e]+(-c)[e]=0$ by distributivity of scalar multiplication. Step 3 gives all the involution and no-fixed-point hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-involution-sum-zero], which now gives the displayed sum equal to zero. Here the monoid is the underlying additive commutative group of that free module; coincident evaluated basis symbols do not change the labeled index set.

lean.statement: theorem mixed_corner_cancellation (a b : ℕ) : (∀ w : Word a b, ∃ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin (a + b)), List.ofFn π = ((List.finRange (a + b)).filter (fun i ↦ w.val[i.val]? = some false)) ++ ((List.finRange (a + b)).filter (fun i ↦ w.val[i.val]? = some true)) ∧ ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (a + b) × Fin (a + b))).filter (fun ij ↦ ij.1 < ij.2 ∧ π ij.2 < π ij.1)).card = inversions w ∧ (π.sign : ℤ) = sign w) ∧ IsEmpty (MixedCorner 0 b) ∧ IsEmpty (MixedCorner a 0) ∧ (0 < a + b → ∃ τ : MixedCorner a b → MixedCorner a b, (∀ p : MixedCorner a b, (τ p).val.2 = p.val.2 ∧ (τ p).val.1.val = (p.val.1.val.set (p.val.2 - 1) (p.val.1.val[p.val.2]?.getD false)).set p.val.2 (p.val.1.val[p.val.2 - 1]?.getD false)) ∧ Function.Involutive τ ∧ (∀ p : MixedCorner a b, τ p ≠ p) ∧ (∀ (p : MixedCorner a b) (ℓ : ℕ), ℓ ≤ a + b → ℓ ≠ p.val.2 → horizontalCount (τ p).val.1 ℓ = horizontalCount p.val.1 ℓ ∧ verticalCount (τ p).val.1 ℓ = verticalCount p.val.1 ℓ) ∧ (∀ p : MixedCorner a b, (inversions (τ p).val.1 = inversions p.val.1 + 1 ∨ inversions p.val.1 = inversions (τ p).val.1 + 1) ∧ sign (τ p).val.1 * (-1 : ℤ) ^ p.val.2 = -(sign p.val.1 * (-1 : ℤ) ^ p.val.2)) ∧ (∀ (X : Type u) (Y : Type v) (x : Fin (a + 1) → X) (y : Fin (b + 1) → Y) (p : MixedCorner a b), (evaluate (τ p).val.1 x y).eraseIdx p.val.2 = (evaluate p.val.1 x y).eraseIdx p.val.2) ∧ ∃ hM : (Set.univ : Set (MixedCorner a b)).Finite, ∀ (X : Type u) (Y : Type v) (x : Fin (a + 1) → X) (y : Fin (b + 1) → Y), (∑ p ∈ hM.toFinset, (sign p.val.1 * (-1 : ℤ) ^ p.val.2) • Finsupp.single ((evaluate p.val.1 x y).eraseIdx p.val.2) (1 : ℤ)) = (0 : List (X × Y) →₀ ℤ))
lean.note: Reuses the already landed horizontal-face module for Word, horizontalCount, verticalCount, inversions, sign and evaluate; the existing definitions are owned by def-sfb-shuffle-word-combinatorics in stmt_deps. The horizontal-face theorem is neither a statement nor a proof dependency. MixedCorner is the literal labeled set introduced by this node. The theorem specifies the horizontal-then-vertical permutation by its complete value list and the swap by two list updates, and includes every prefix, inversion, sign, evaluation, sum and empty-axis clause. Finiteness is an existential conclusion, not an added hypothesis. The ambient free module on lists contains exactly the length-n strings occurring in the sum.
